# Circuit overlap bodies: localization, exact multiplicity, and a zero-charge obstruction

This note concerns finite positive cap circuits and actual positive-volume
fibers. It does not turn the grouped-cap certificate into an OC proof.
The final example shows precisely why its additional nonnegative term
cannot by itself supply the missing constant.

Write gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j for j>=1. Let K be a d-dimensional convex
body, d>=2, of volume w. Consider k=r+1 nonzero continuous normals
u_j of rank r, with their unique positive dependence normalized as
sum_j lambda_j u_j=0, lambda_j>0, sum_j lambda_j=1. Let

    L_j(x)=u_j.x+e_j,
    c=sum_j lambda_j e_j,
    H_j={L_j>=0},
    A=intersection_j H_j.

We call A the overlap body; when r<d it can be a cylinder. Assume c>=0.

## 1. Exact overlap geometry and recentering

The image of the linear map U:x -> (u_j.x)_j is the r-dimensional
hyperplane orthogonal to lambda. Thus the equations L_j(x)=c for every
j have a solution: the target vector (c-e_j)_j is orthogonal to lambda.
In particular A is nonempty. If c>0 it has nonempty interior.

The weighted margin sum is identically c, so the H_j cover all of R^d.
Their common recession cone is exactly ker U. Indeed, u_j.v>=0 for
all j and sum lambda_j u_j.v=0 force all u_j.v=0. It follows that A
is a bounded r-simplex in a complement of ker U, plus ker U, if c>0.
For c=0 it is the affine solution space of L_j=0.

Every y in A yields a new through-y cover

    H'_j(y)={x:u_j.(x-y)>=0} subset H_j.                  (1)

The inclusion follows from L_j(y)>=0. The positive dependence proves
that these new halfspaces still cover all of R^d. This holds for EVERY
point in A, rather than only one arbitrarily selected contact.

For r=d and c>0, choose any d normals, say the first d. They are linearly
independent by minimality. The map x -> (lambda_j L_j(x))_(j<=d)
sends A to {t_j>=0, sum_j t_j<=c}, so

    |A| = c^d / (d! |det(u_1,...,u_d)| product_(j<=d)lambda_j). (2)

Here the normals are the rows of the displayed determinant. This formula
tracks arbitrary positive rescalings of the original cap margins.

## 2. The entire overlap lies in a controlled region of K

Put beta=max_j |K intersect H_j|/w. Apply the common-contact theorem to
(1). Its hypotheses hold for every y in A. In particular:

* beta>=gamma_d;
* if beta<gamma_(d-1), then A subset int K;
* for every y in A, depth_K(y)>=1-beta/gamma_(d-1).

The second assertion follows from the external-contact dimension drop:
an exterior or boundary y would force an original cap fraction at least
gamma_(d-1). The third assertion follows by applying the same theorem
to the complement in K of a shallowest through-y cap. These are the
proved results in `candidate a20765b75f4bd3ee`.

Since a rank-deficient A contains a line, the second assertion also
shows that beta<gamma_(d-1) forces r=d. This conclusion requires no
conditioning bound on the normal matrix.

The explicit rigidity theorem in
`candidate e81e0e86f9a482f3` further gives,
when beta<gamma_(d-1),

    A subset g + R(K-K),
    R = d^2 (beta-gamma_d)/(gamma_(d-1)-beta),             (3)

where g is the ordinary centroid of K. Its proof is separately audited
in `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

For a full-rank circuit with c>0, put

    v=(|A|/|K-K|)^(1/d)>0.

Volume in (3) gives v<=R. Rearranging, or treating beta>=gamma_(d-1)
directly, yields the unconditional quantitative inequality

    beta >= (d^2 gamma_d + v gamma_(d-1))/(d^2+v)
          = gamma_d + (gamma_(d-1)-gamma_d) v/(d^2+v).     (4)

Thus a positive-volume overlap forces a strictly larger largest cap
than gamma_d. Formula (2) makes its dependence on the circuit margin
and normal determinant completely explicit. No comparison between
different fibers, or between different circuits' determinants, is made.

## 3. Exact multiplicity charge on mixed fibers

Pointwise on R^d,

    sum_j 1_(H_j) >= 1 + r 1_A.                          (5)

Outside A the cover supplies at least one cap; inside A every one of
the r+1 caps is present. Consequently

    sum_j |K intersect H_j| >= w + r |K intersect A|.     (6)

All sets here are closed. Their boundary hyperplanes have d-volume
zero; (5) itself is also valid on boundaries, without deleting them.

For a finite mixed set with full d-dimensional fibers K_z, let circuits
i have ranks r_i and margins c_i(z)>=0 on an assigned partition B_i
of the nonempty integer fibers. They therefore cover the whole
continuous space at every assigned index. Write A_i(z) for their
overlap body. Summing (6), and retaining the nonnegative cap masses
over unassigned fibers on the left, gives

    sum_i sum_(j in circuit i) mu(H_ij)
      >= M + sum_i r_i sum_(z in B_i) |K_z intersect A_i(z)|.  (7)

If every cap has total mixed mass <T, then

    T sum_i(r_i+1)
      > M + sum_i r_i sum_(z in B_i) |K_z intersect A_i(z)|.  (8)

Caps reused in several circuits are counted with their occurrences on
both sides of the first expression; this does not incorrectly identify
their masses as disjoint. The strict inequality only uses the finite
number of occurrences and the assumed strict individual budget.

## 4. The extra charge can vanish under full parity and contact conditions

The explicit convex-body example in
`candidate d0f838592db846be` supplies four rank-two
circuits and six positive two-dimensional integer fibers. Their base
support is

    {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}.

Its four parity witnesses are the binary square. The three fibers in
the root-(1,1) basin are squares of radius 1/10 with centers
(3,-1), (-1,3), (-1,-1). The other root fibers are squares of radius
1/100 with centers (11,-5), (7,-1), (7,-5). These are exactly the
integer fibers of the full-dimensional convex hull of those six
embedded squares, as proved in the cited note.

Every circuit uses normals (1,0), (0,1), (-1,-1), with margins
u_j.x+ell_i(z), where

    ell_00=1/100-(z_1+z_2)/10,
    ell_10=(z_1-z_2)/10-1/20,
    ell_01=(z_2-z_1)/10-1/20,
    ell_11=(z_1+z_2)/10-1/10.

For EVERY circuit i, its first cap contains the entire fiber (1,1)
and all three small root fibers; its second cap contains precisely the
entire fiber (2,1); its third contains precisely the entire fiber (1,2).
Every unintended incidence is strictly excluded. Therefore

    sum_j 1_(H_ij)(z,x)=1 for every (z,x) in S,
    K_z intersect A_i(z)=empty for all i,z.              (9)

In particular, all the additional charges in (7) and (8) vanish
identically, including for the canonical parity-forest assignment.
Nevertheless this example has the full set of four parity witnesses,
strict expanded-facet contacts, a bounded full-dimensional auxiliary
mixed-lattice-free polytope, and all cross-contact inequalities.
Those verifications and their exact arithmetic are in the cited note
and `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_parity_forest_cap_transport.py`.

This example's cap budget is NOT below the OC target. Equation (9)
therefore does not refute OC or a use of its hypothesized small budget.
It does show that parity witnesses, circuit rank, cross-contacts and
convex fiber compatibility alone cannot make the overlap correction
positive. A further source-mass allocation argument remains necessary.
